cannotTest: The rule governs process and git history, not file content: it requires that when code already merged into master is edited additively, characterization tests are created BEFORE the edit. Deciding it needs (a) knowing whether the touched code is merged into master (including via ancestry), (b) judging whether a change is additive vs. intentional behaviour change, and (c) verifying commit/ordering that tests were authored first. A per-line regex cannot decide any of this, and no shell command can reliably distinguish a compliant additive change from a normal refactor without firing on legitimate work. Reviewers must judge this rule from commit history and PR ordering.
